transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-16
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes (recorded)
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Jonah Rivera (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Calypso - Head ML Ops), Daniel Cho (Calypso - Platform Eng), Lina Gomez (Calypso - SRE)
Shared links: pricing sketch placeholder <link: redwood/pricing/Calypso-Uplift-2026.xlsx>, pilot runbook draft <link: redwood/pilots/calypso-vpc-runbook.md>, SOC2 snapshot <link: redwood/security/soc2-2025.pdf>

Summary:
Quick check-in to confirm renewal uplift sizing, APAC edge activation status, pilot scope for private VPC run, and next steps for SLA/pricing. Some back-and-forth on latency expectations vs cost; customer wants a firm uplift number and timeline for APAC activation.

Topics: retainer uplift, APAC edge activation, private VPC pilot, SOC2/audit, performance benchmarks, timeline

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: okay good afternoon everyone, thanks for joining, um this is Maya from Redwood, with Jonah on the call as well. how are you folks doing
[00:06] Priya: doing well thanks, busy quarter but this is timely for us so appreciate the readout
[00:10] Jonah: hey, hi Priya, hi Daniel, Lina, thanks for carving out time. quick agenda — pricing sketch, APAC edge status, pilot details, perf targets and next steps.
[00:22] Daniel: sounds good. real quick, Priya asked me to join because we have infra questions about the VPC peering and the egress paths into our KMS.
[00:30] Priya: yes and also data residency — we need to ensure logs and telemetry from APAC stay in-region for the first 12 months.
[00:38] Maya: absolutely, that's on the table. um just to orient, today we'll propose a 250% retainer uplift to support the extra reserved capacity in APAC plus burst, and discuss a pilot plan for private VPC on-prem-ish setup. is that aligned?
[00:52] Priya: aligned, but 250% feels high on paper, we need to see tradeoffs on latency improvements vs incremental cost.
[00:58] Jonah: yeah and we'll show the latency delta between hosted and dedicated APAC nodes — small models are almost real-time, big context L2+ can show higher variance.
[01:10] Lina: can I interrupt, quick operational note — our SREs care about connection churn, the last vendor we tried had spikes during prefix cache warmup and that killed a downstream job.
[01:21] Jonah: good call, Lina. Redwood's caching/kv approach is automatic but we've been pushing improvements to vsync on cold starts — we can pin config so warmup is staggered. i'll add a config appendix to the runbook.
[01:33] Daniel: when you say pin config, is that something in the customer console or part of the private deployment?
[01:38] Jonah: depends — for hosted + dedicated we expose console toggles; for private VPC we'll surface the same options via the control plane but you run the code path in your environment. sometimes the transcript messes with the product name — we call it Redwood Private, but i've heard it come out as "Redwood Dedicate" on other calls, sorry for the slip.
[01:55] Priya: (laughs) okay noted.
[01:58] Maya: can i run through the numbers quick? current retainer is 10k tokens/sec equivalent, and you folks have a seasonal spike pattern where 40% of traffic originates from APAC hours. to give consistent tail latency we recommend reserving an APAC block that's 2.5x your baseline APAC traffic which is the 250% uplift.
[02:18] Priya: baseline numbers — yes, our current baseline is approx 4k tokens/sec average across APAC window, peak around 9k for short bursts.
[02:26] Maya: thanks. so the uplift would cover peak headroom and smooth the queuing; without it we can rely on cross-region failover but that increases p99 latency by 120-200ms depending on model.
[02:38] Daniel: what's the showstopper for us? is it cost or compliance or both?
[02:43] Priya: both, really. cost needs to be justified to finance but compliance — logs must remain in region. plus our risk team wants to avoid cross-region KV cache leakage.
[02:54] Jonah: right, the KV cache is per-region in our design, unless you opt into global cache which you won't for this use case. so regionally isolated cache + VPC peering + KMS in-region is doable. i will call out the exact KMS integration path — we support customer-managed keys and HSM via standard provider connectors; sometimes the transcription spells HSM as 'h-s-m' but it's the same.
[03:17] Lina: how about failover — if APAC nodes get saturated do you route to US-West? we need predictable behavior under overload.
[03:24] Jonah: yes, smart routing is policy-based — you can set strict latency-first which will prefer local nodes even if cost higher, or cost-aware which prefers cheaper cross-region fallback. we suggest latency-first for production-critical flows and cost-aware for background tasks.
[03:36] Priya: finance will push cost-aware though. can you quantify cost delta between the two policies?
[03:42] Maya: we'll include a delta table in the pricing sketch — rough ballpark is +18-30% for latency-first for the APAC edge block depending on token mix and batching; exact numbers in the spreadsheet.
[03:53] Daniel: okay. pilot plan — what's the minimum to validate?
[03:57] Jonah: suggest a 4-week private pilot in your VPC with a small reserved pool — we run benchmark sweeps for p50/p95/p99 across typical prompt lengths, simulate warmup cycles, and validate failover behavior. goal is to prove 90% of calls meet p95 SLA under intended QPS.
[04:15] Priya: timeline-wise can we start week of 6/22? we have an infra freeze the week before.
[04:20] Maya: that should work if we get signoff and the prelim artifacts this week — pricing sketch and pilot runbook go out by 6/18, Jonah's benchmark plan by 6/21, then onboarding sync the 22nd.
[04:31] Lina: regarding telemetry — we want redacted logs only, not raw prompts. is that supported?
[04:35] Jonah: yes, redaction hooks are supported; there is a minor agent-side configuration for the private deployment. we'll include sample redaction regex and a helm snippet in the runbook.
[04:45] Priya: tokens and billing model — will we be billed for tokens that are redacted or only for model compute?
[04:50] Maya: billing is per-token consumed by model; telemetry redaction doesn't change compute charges unless you also cache prefixes that reduce token usage. we'll point to the detailed billing appendix.
[04:58] Daniel: any legal checkpoints? we have to run a vendor risk assessment; need SOC2 and data flow diagrams.
[05:04] Maya: we have SOC2 Type II and ISO snapshot attached in the shared link. we'll add a simple data flow diagram for the VPC/pod network.
[05:12] Priya: competitors — we've run MacroServe and briefly tested ZephyrAI. MacroServe had cheaper list prices but higher latencies, Zephyr had good latency but missing enterprise features. just flagging that we'll do side-by-side.
[05:24] Jonah: understood, we'll propose a small benchmark that mirrors your MacroServe tests so you can compare apples-to-apples.
[05:30] Lina: one more ops ask — SLA credits calculation, how strict are the p99 targets and do you offer automatic fallback?
[05:36] Maya: SLA credits are standard in the enterprise addendum; for p99 we can tune the SLO per model surface. automatic fallback is configurable — we can enable or disable to match your risk profile.
[05:45] Priya: okay. let's talk numbers quickly on the call - can you confirm the monthly committed spend ballpark for the uplift?
[05:51] Maya: ballpark for 2.5x APAC reserved block + baseline commit looks like $120k/month, but final depends on exact token mix and retention choices — we'll send a line-itemed sketch.
[06:03] Daniel: that's higher than we expected but maybe acceptable for peak season. finance will ask if there's a stepped plan so we don't immediately take full uplift.
[06:11] Maya: we can propose a 2-step commit: 1) immediate 1.5x uplift for first 3 months, 2) step to full 2.5x after performance validation. we'll outline both options in the pricing doc.
[06:24] Priya: that staged approach sounds workable. also can we include a clause for making adjustments after 90 days if actual traffic deviates by >20%?
[06:32] Maya: yes that's a reasonable amendment, we'll include a traffic variance clause.
[06:36] Lina: on the APAC activation, what's the expected lead time once we sign?
[06:40] Jonah: if you sign and choose hosted dedicated APAC, we can provision in ~10 business days; for private VPC it's about 3 weeks to run the on-site tests and KMS handoff.
[06:52] Priya: we prefer private VPC for now. finance will need cost + timeline to decide.
[06:58] Maya: noted. next steps recap: Maya sends pricing + SLA + dataflow + certs by 6/18; Jonah sends pilot runbook and benchmark matrix by 6/21; Priya to share traffic traces by 6/19. onboarding sync week of 6/22.
[07:18] Daniel: small nit — for the pilot, can we schedule a 1hr dry run with our SREs before the formal start? we want to exercise the peering and auth flow.
[07:26] Jonah: yes we'll do a dry run 48 hours before. i'll include that in the runbook timeline.
[07:30] Priya: great. any other concerns?
[07:34] Lina: nothing else from infra.
[07:36] Maya: okay thanks everyone. i'll follow up with the spreadsheet and notes. thanks for the candid feedback.
[07:42] Priya: thanks.
[07:43] Meeting close.

Notes on transcription quality: there are minor mis-attributions, occasional filler words and vendor/product names mis-spelled (e.g., "Redwood Dedicate"), timestamps are approximate.

Final recap (in transcript):

- Private VPC pilot planned; dry run 48h before pilot; pilot start target week of 6/22.
- Action owners: Maya/Jonah/Priya with due dates in the action items list.
- Next meeting likely after pilot dry run or when pricing is reviewed by finance.
